keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox "c. 5000 BC - c. 4000 BC"; "Lengyel pottery was found in western Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Austria, Poland, and Slovenia"; "Several Sopot culture finds in Croatia and Hungary were dated to the same general periods". Moravia is drawn from 5000 BCE ("Austrian/Moravian Painted Ware I and II"), the rest of Czechia (Bohemia) and central Poland are not: the page puts "Stroke-ornamented ware ... adjacent to the north" and the Linear Pottery page gives the Stroked Pottery culture "5000-4500 BC", so linear-pottery-culture holds them until 4500 BCE (this dossier gains them then). Slavonia: the Sopot culture page says it was "first identified in eastern Slavonia" and that it "helped Lengyel culture start" in Transdanubia; the Lengyel page itself says only that "Several Sopot culture finds in Croatia and Hungary were dated to the same general periods" and lists Slovenia, not Croatia, among the countries of Lengyel pottery, so Slavonia is drawn on the Sopot page's word (confidence 2). No area figure to compare.

correction.text: the Middle Danube core and Bohemia (phase IV, the "Jordanow/Jordansmühler culture") after central Poland passed to the Funnelbeaker

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Middle Danube core and Bohemia after the Funnelbeaker emerged in the north c. 4100 BCE (Funnelbeaker page) and took central Poland. Bohemia stays to the end: "It flourished from 5000 to 4000 BC, ending with phase IV, e.g., in Bohemia represented by the 'Jordanow/Jordansmühler culture'"; the page says the Lengyel "In its northern extent, overlapped the somewhat later but otherwise approximately contemporaneous Funnelbeaker culture", and funnelbeaker-culture_-4100 also draws Bohemia, so Bohemia is drawn by both 4100..4000 (a page-backed overlap, flagged in the notes).

region.text: the Middle Danube: Transdanubia, Moravia, Austria, Slovakia, Slovenia and Slavonia

ledger.note: 5000 BCE: the painted-pottery Lengyel culture succeeds the LBK on the middle Danube. "It flourished from 5000 to 4000 BC"; "The Lengyel culture was preceded by the Linear Pottery culture"; "Also closely related are the Stroke-ornamented ware and Rössen cultures, adjacent to the north and west". Bohemia, Kuyavia and Greater Poland are not part of the 5000 BCE shape: the Stroked Pottery culture ("5000-4500 BC") holds them until 4500 BCE. Slavonia: the Sopot culture page says it was "first identified in eastern Slavonia" and that it "helped Lengyel culture start" in Transdanubia; the Lengyel page itself says only that "Several Sopot culture finds in Croatia and Hungary were dated to the same general periods" and lists Slovenia, not Croatia, among the countries of Lengyel pottery, so Slavonia is drawn on the Sopot page's word (confidence 2).

region.text: the northern extent: Bohemia (phase IV, the "Jordanow/Jordansmühler culture") and central Poland (Osłonki)

ledger.note: 4500 BCE: the northern extent, Bohemia (phase IV, the "Jordanow/Jordansmühler culture") and central Poland (Osłonki), enters the Lengyel after the Stroked Pottery culture. The Lengyel page does not date it (page silent): "Also closely related are the Stroke-ornamented ware and Rössen cultures, adjacent to the north and west, respectively"; the Linear Pottery page gives "Stroked Pottery culture (Stichbandkeramik (SBK), 5000-4500 BC)". The year is the end of the Stroked Pottery culture.

region.text: central Poland (Osłonki): Kuyavian-Pomeranian and Greater Poland

ledger.note: 4100 BCE: the Funnelbeaker culture takes central Poland (Kuyavia, Greater Poland). "In its northern extent, overlapped the somewhat later but otherwise approximately contemporaneous Funnelbeaker culture"; the Funnelbeaker page: "emerged in northern modern-day Germany c. 4100 BCE" with the Lengyel among its predecessors. The page dates Osłonki "4100 BC" and "c. 4000 BC" captions in Poland, so Lengyel presence there to 4000 is possible; the hand-over stays at 4100 (confidence 2). Bohemia is not handed over here: "ending with phase IV, e.g., in Bohemia represented by the Jordanow/Jordansmühler culture", so it stays to the 4000 BCE end although funnelbeaker-culture_-4100 also draws it (page-backed overlap).

ledger.note: 4000 BCE: the Lengyel ends with phase IV. Infobox end c. 4000 BC, "ending with phase IV, e.g., in Bohemia represented by the 'Jordanow/Jordansmühler culture'"; infobox "Followed by: Funnelbeaker culture, Baden culture, Globular Amphora culture" while the body says "succeeded by the Corded Ware culture"; the Baden and Globular Amphora have no dossier, so the middle Danube goes to nobody. Bohemia is already drawn by the Funnelbeaker from 4100 BCE (overlap), so its part of the dissolve changes no map owner.

notes:
Culture dossier, one page. The page's successors disagree (infobox Funnelbeaker/Baden/Globular Amphora vs body Corded Ware). The Tiszapolgár and Baden cultures of the Carpathian Basin after 4500/4000 BCE have no dossier (gap). Gazetteer: Lengyel, Osłonki are not places; "Transdanubia" is not a region; admin-1 lists stand in.

Repair 2026-10-18 (after the reviewer): the keyframe from 5000 BCE no longer draws Bohemia, Kuyavian-Pomeranian and Greater Poland, which linear-pottery-culture (Stroked Pottery, '5000-4500 BC') holds to 4500 BCE; a new keyframe lengyel-culture_-4500 and a gain in 4500 BCE (counterpart linear-pottery-culture, confidence 1, page silent) bring them in. Moravia stays from 5000 BCE and linear-pottery-culture drops it. Following the reviewer's advisory, only Kuyavia and Greater Poland pass to the Funnelbeaker in 4100 BCE and Bohemia stays to the 4000 BCE end (Lengyel page: 'ending with phase IV, e.g., in Bohemia represented by the Jordanow/Jordansmuhler culture'). Consequence: funnelbeaker-culture_-4100 (another author's file, verdict fix, untouched) also draws Bohemia, so about 233 cells are drawn by both 4100..4000; the Lengyel page says it 'overlapped the somewhat later but otherwise approximately contemporaneous Funnelbeaker culture' in its northern extent, so the overlap is page-backed; the Funnelbeaker's author may start Bohemia in 4000 BCE instead. I am less sure about Poland: the page's captions 'Burial with copper items, Oslonki, Poland, 4100 BC' and 'Copper axe, Poland, c. 4000 BC' could support Lengyel presence there to 4000 too; I keep the 4100 hand-over at confidence 2 because the Funnelbeaker page dates its emergence c. 4100 BCE and the page does not say the captioned objects are Lengyel rather than Funnelbeaker-contemporary. Slavonia (thin finding): the Sopot culture page says it was 'first identified in eastern Slavonia' and 'helped Lengyel culture start'; it does not say Sopot is a Lengyel variant, and the Lengyel page names only Slovenia, not Croatia, for Lengyel pottery, so Slavonia is a reading from the Sopot page (dated 'c. 5,500 BC - c. 3,800 BC' in its infobox, 'around 5000 BC' in its text).
